model Server {
  id                  String        @id @default(cuid())
  name                String
  label               String? // customer-facing nickname (rename)
  hostname            String
  vmid                Int?          @unique
  status              ServerStatus  @default(PENDING)
  ipAddress           String?       @unique
  sshPort             Int?          @unique
  rootPassword        String?
  rootPasswordEnc     String?
  isFree              Boolean       @default(false)
  autoRenew           Boolean       @default(true)
  gameVariant         String? // game-server type/loader (e.g. paper, carbon, bepinex) — see lib/game-config
  gameConfig          Json? // per-game settings values (validated against the family schema)
  suspendedNote       String?
  // WHY a server is suspended: "UNPAID" | "ABUSE" | "ADMIN". Null = never suspended.
  //
  // `suspendedNote` used to be the only signal, and nothing consumed it, so every
  // suspension looked identical to the billing engine. Two live consequences:
  // (1) `terminateOverdue` selected on `status: "SUSPENDED"` alone, while the
  //     renewal sweep EXCLUDES suspended servers — so an admin suspending a
  //     paid-up customer pending an investigation meant they were never charged,
  //     never warned, their term lapsed, and 13 days later their VM and all its
  //     data were destroyed with a "prolonged non-payment" notice they had never
  //     been given a chance to act on.
  // (2) `renewNow` auto-unsuspended ANY suspended server on payment, so a spammer
  //     suspended for outbound abuse could pay and put themselves straight back
  //     on the network.
  // Both now scope strictly to UNPAID.
  suspendReason       String?
  expiresAt           DateTime?
  // ---- Dunning (failed auto-charge retry state) ----
  // dunningStage counts CARD ATTEMPTS THAT HAVE FAILED for the current unpaid
  // period: 0 = nothing owed / paid, 1..N = that many failures. Reset to 0 the
  // moment a renewal succeeds. `dunningNextAt` gates the next retry so a
  // 5-minute billing sweep cannot burn every retry in a quarter of an hour, and
  // `dunningPayUrl` is a hosted Checkout link emailed to the customer so they can
  // clear the balance themselves (also how 3-D Secure challenges are satisfied).
  dunningStage        Int           @default(0)
  dunningNextAt       DateTime?
  dunningPayUrl       String?
  createdAt           DateTime      @default(now())
  updatedAt           DateTime      @updatedAt
  userId              String
model Board {
  id        String        @id @default(cuid())
  name      String
  appId     String?
  app       App?          @relation(fields: [appId], references: [id], onDelete: SetNull)
  createdAt DateTime      @default(now())
  columns   BoardColumn[]
  cards     Card[]

  @@index([appId])
}

model BoardColumn {
  id       String  @id @default(cuid())
  boardId  String
  board    Board   @relation(fields: [boardId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  name     String
  position Int     @default(0)
  cards    Card[]

  @@index([boardId])
}

model Card {
  id          String           @id @default(cuid())
  boardId     String
  board       Board            @relation(fields: [boardId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  columnId    String
  column      BoardColumn      @relation(fields: [columnId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  title       String
  description String           @default("") // markdown
  type        CardType         @default(FEATURE)
  priority    CardPriority     @default(NORMAL)
  labels      String[]         @default([])
  assignee    String? // free-text ("me", "claude", a name)
  position    Int              @default(0)
  archivedAt  DateTime?
  createdAt   DateTime         @default(now())
  updatedAt   DateTime         @updatedAt
  attachments CardAttachment[]
  comments    CardComment[]

  @@index([boardId])
  @@index([columnId])
}

model CardAttachment {
  id         String         @id @default(cuid())
  cardId     String
  card       Card           @relation(fields: [cardId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  filename   String // original name shown to the user
  storedName String // on-disk name (uuid + ext) under the board upload dir
  mime       String         @default("application/octet-stream")
  sizeBytes  Int            @default(0)
  kind       AttachmentKind @default(FILE)
  createdAt  DateTime       @default(now())

  @@index([cardId])
}

model CardComment {
  id         String   @id @default(cuid())
  cardId     String
  card       Card     @relation(fields: [cardId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  authorName String   @default("")
  body       String
  createdAt  DateTime @default(now())

  @@index([cardId])
}

#
#  A full, ISOLATED copy of the production stack for testing. Nothing here

#    • container names  → soulpilates-staging-*   (prod uses soulpilates-prod-*)

  mongo:
    image: mongo:8
    container_name: soulpilates-staging-mongo
    restart: unless-stopped

Everything is verified and cleaned up. Here is the final report.

## Result

**Task complete.** Manual/desk bookings in the Soul Pilates CRM now send the client the same booking-confirmation email the online path sends. Built and deployed to STAGING only; prod fully untouched.

### Manual create paths found (all in `SoulPilates.Services/SchedulingService.cs`)
The task's "verified fact" (email called only from `CustomerAuthService`) was **stale** — the email is also sent by `PaymentService.FireAndForgetBookingEmail` (the real online path) and by both reschedule paths. I traced every booking-create route from the controllers down:
- `ReserveSpotAsync` (BookingSource=ONLINE) → creates a **RESERVED** row, no email. Online confirmation is sent by `PaymentService` at the RESERVED→BOOKED transition (Stripe/credit/zero-amount).
- `AdminRescheduleBookingAsync` + `CustomerAuthService` reschedule → already email.
- **The three MANUAL paths that create a BOOKED row directly and never emailed:** `BookClientAsync` (staff credit book, ADMIN), `WalkInCheckoutAsync` (POS walk-in, WALK_IN), `AdminAddStudentAsync` (admin/instructor add-to-session, WALK_IN).

### How double-sending is prevented
Online bookings are RESERVED first and emailed by PaymentService — they **never** flow through the three manual methods (which create BOOKED directly). Email was added only in those manual methods, so online customers still get exactly one email. `SplitBookingAsync` (seat redistribution of an already-created booking) was deliberately left out of scope.

### Files changed
- `SoulPilates.Services/SchedulingService.cs` (+59 lines): new fire-and-forget helper `FireAndForgetManualBookingEmail(attendance, session)`, guarded on non-empty email, resolving email/name from the Client record when the attendance doesn't carry them (BookClient/AdminAddStudent only store clientId). Wired into all three manual paths. No DI/constructor change needed — `IEmailService` and the Clients collection were already injected.
